text:
## Observations

1. Transposing the grid swaps right and down in every path and preserves its weight, so the grid can be oriented with \(\min(H,W)\) columns.
2. A forward path sum depends only on the cell above and the cell to the left, while a backward path sum depends only on the cell below and the cell to the right.
3. When Takahashi moves to an adjacent row, the row he leaves is the only row that needs a new cached sum. A move within a row leaves all cached sums outside that row valid.
4. Every path crosses from the current row to the row below exactly once, unless the current row is the last row.
5. The algorithm uses only addition and multiplication modulo \(998244353\), so zero weights and repeated assignments need no special handling.

## Solution sketch

1. “Transposing the grid swaps right and down in every path and preserves its weight, so the grid can be oriented with \(\min(H,W)\) columns.”

   Transpose if \(W>H\). If transposed, swap the starting row and column and translate the movement directions by swapping \(L\) with \(U\) and \(R\) with \(D\). Let \(k=\min(H,W)\) be the resulting number of columns.

2. “A forward path sum depends only on the cell above and the cell to the left, while a backward path sum depends only on the cell below and the cell to the right.”

   Cache forward sums for all rows strictly above Takahashi and backward sums for all rows strictly below him. A forward sum includes the weight of its ending cell. Compute it by multiplying that weight by the sum of the forward values from above and from the left. A backward sum includes the weight of its starting cell and uses the analogous recurrence with values from below and from the right. Build the forward rows top to bottom and left to right, and build the backward rows bottom to top and right to left. Treat missing neighbors as zero, with a virtual \(1\) directly above the top-left cell and directly below the bottom-right cell to start the two recurrences.

3. “When Takahashi moves to an adjacent row, the row he leaves is the only row that needs a new cached sum. A move within a row leaves all cached sums outside that row valid.”

   Before assigning the destination cell, handle any row change. On a downward move, compute the forward sums for the row Takahashi is leaving using the weights currently in that row. On an upward move, compute its backward sums instead. The destination row is now the current row, so its old cache is no longer needed. On a horizontal move, skip this cache update. Move to the destination and apply the assignment there.

4. “Every path crosses from the current row to the row below exactly once, unless the current row is the last row.”

   After the assignment, compute the current row’s forward sums from left to right. If there is a row below, multiply each forward sum by the cached backward sum in the same column one row below, then add the products. Each product joins a prefix and a suffix across one downward edge, with each cell weight counted once. If the current row is the last row, take the forward sum at its rightmost cell. Print the result modulo \(998244353\).

5. “The algorithm uses only addition and multiplication modulo \(998244353\), so zero weights and repeated assignments need no special handling.”

   Apply the same update and answer procedure for all \(Q\) changes, including revisits and assignments of zero. Initialization takes \(O(HW)\) time. Each change requires at most two scans of \(k\) cells, for \(O(HW+Q\min(H,W))\) total time. The grid and cached sums use \(O(HW)\) space when changes are processed as they are read.

generation.note: Harness wall time includes Codex startup; not API latency.

usage.note: Codex token counts include its harness context; not comparable to API usage.

isolation.mechanism: codex exec, fresh ephemeral session, empty temporary working directory, user config and exec rules ignored, read-only sandbox, web search and listed features disabled, credential-like variables removed from the environment
isolation.limits: Codex harness instructions and its own tool descriptions remain in the model context; they cannot be removed. Tool isolation is verified post hoc from the event stream, which contained no tool, command, file or search events.
